item.strong: SRS v1 · UPI Payments Application for Bank Customers

srs.title: UPI Payments Application for Bank Customers
srs.summary: Develop a secure UPI payments application enabling customers to send/receive money and scan QR codes at merchants. The system must enforce strict ₹50,000 limits per Electronic Wallet (E-Wallet), excluding transaction amounts exceeding this threshold. Integrate central bank fraud monitoring rules (e-
assumptions: The regulatory body explicitly mandates standard fraud rules from a central feed, relieving the bank of custom rule creation.
The business accepts no appeal process; accounts with failed logins or suspicious activity are auto-blocked without human review.
The term 'E3' corresponds to Electronic Wallets (E-Wallets) as defined in RBI guidelines.
The regulatory feed provided by the central bank will be available in a machine-readable format suitable for real-time integration.
stakeholders: Bank IT/Engineering Team: Responsible for API integration with the central bank fraud feed and QR payment infrastructure.
Regulatory Authority (Central Bank): Source of mandatory fraud rules and transaction limit mandates.
Compliance/Anti-Fraud Unit: Responsible for periodic review of limits and monitoring of breaches (though execution is automated in this scope).
Merchant Partners: Providers of QR code services.
Customer Support: Handles notification delivery for failed logins/alerts (though no manual intervention occurs).

requirements.statement: The system must enforce a strict daily transaction limit of ₹50,000 per E3 per user and automatically reject any structured transaction attempts (multiple small transactions) that aggregate to this or
requirements.acceptance: The system rejects the transaction with an error message citing E3 compliance when the aggregation of the current transaction plus pending transactions in the current day exceeds ₹

requirements.statement: The system must import and apply pre-defined standard fraud monitoring rules from the central bank feed rather than allowing customer-defined custom rules.
requirements.acceptance: During system configuration, the application successfully imports rule sets labeled as 'Standard Central Bank Feed' and flags any attempt to save a non-standard rule as invalid.

requirements.statement: The system must configure fraud detection rules to monitor transaction velocity (e.g., fund transfers, cash withdrawals) within a defined short period as mandated by E1.
requirements.acceptance: The system generates an alert within the system defined short period (e.g., 15 minutes) whenever a user exceeds the velocity threshold defined by the imported standard rules.

requirements.statement: The system must detect and alert for high-risk Merchant Category Codes (MCC) based on the parameters provided in the standard fraud rule feed.
requirements.acceptance: The system successfully flags and alerts when a transaction matches a high-risk MCC parameter defined in the active standard rule set.

requirements.statement: The system must implement an automated rejection and account blocking mechanism for failed log-in attempts without requiring human intervention for approval.
requirements.acceptance: Upon a failure to unlock an account that exceeds the maximum number of allowed failed authentication attempts defined in the standard rules, the system immediately denies the login

requirements.statement: The system must enforce blocking of user access if the number of failed log-in attempts reaches the limit defined in the standard rules, and must notify the customer via SMS or email.
requirements.acceptance: When the failed attempt counter hits the limit defined in the active configuration, the system transitions the account to 'Blocked' status and triggers an SMS/email notification to

requirements.statement: The system must ensure that all sensitive card details (PAN, CVV, etc.) are encrypted or tokenized in storage and never persisted in plain text at the system or vendor level as per E2.
requirements.acceptance: A security scan of the production database confirms zero instances of card details stored in plain text format; all fields utilize encryption algorithms meeting industry standards.

requirements.statement: The system must monitor card transaction limits at the Card Network switch level for both domestic and international transactions separately as mandated by E2.
requirements.acceptance: The system demonstrates successful integration with the Card Network switch API, showing distinct limit configurations and breach alerts for domestic and international

requirements.statement: The system must execute a continuous 24x7 surveillance and monitoring cycle for suspicious transactions, including weekends and long holidays, as required by E2.
requirements.acceptance: System logs and monitoring dashboards show zero downtime and continuous processing of suspicious transaction alerts 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, verified by automated uptime

requirements.statement: The system must include a periodic review mechanism to adjust transaction limits and fraud rules based on a Board-approved risk appetite policy.
requirements.acceptance: The system provides a scheduled job that executes a periodic review of all transaction limits and rule parameters, comparing them against the current Board-approved policy document
